note: Famous trees Commons has a category for and we do not map. Found by scripts/famous_trees.py; each one already has photographs and usually coordinates, so the expensive half of a research pass is done. Not verified by us, not published. 2026-09-03 verify pass: 3 Giessen candidates (Adam und Eva, Alte Eiche Roedgen, Schillerlinde Roedgen) and 2 Rudolstadt candidates (Freundschaftseiche, Einheitslinde) verified but held below the 4-tree floor; full write-ups in data/leads/giessen.json and data/leads/rudolstadt.json. Symbolic oaks in Germany blocked as a category, not a single tree. Entries removed from this leads list now that they are delivered elsewhere. 2026-09-03 follow-up verify pass: found the 4th Giessen tree, Lindengruppe an der Lindbachquelle (Lützellinden, also a Gießen district), which clears Giessen to the 4-tree floor; all 4 delivered to data/research/giessen-verified.json (gie_001-gie_004), and data/leads/giessen.json emptied accordingly. No fourth Rudolstadt candidate was found. Three further candidates verified and delivered as single-tree-destination exceptions (2026-08-31 ruling), each a nationally or regionally famous named lime with official protection and a real reason someone would travel specifically for it: Linde in Reinborn (data/research/reinborn-verified.json, rbn_001, 14.34m girth), Tanzlinde (Effeltrich) (data/research/effeltrich-verified.json, eff_001, Nationalerbe-Baum No. 39), and Schenklengsfelder Dorflinde (data/research/schenklengsfeld-verified.json, sfd_001, 17.91m girth, possibly Germany's oldest deciduous tree). One candidate, Gerichtslinde (Klingenberg am Main), verified as alive and existing but judged NOT to clear the single-tree exception (modest 4.22m girth, no official protection found, folk age claim of 800y unsupported by its own register's 325y dendrological estimate); written up in data/leads/klingenberg-am-main.json. All 5 of these entries removed from this leads list now that they are handled. 2026-09-03 second follow-up verify pass: two further single candidates verified and held below the 4-tree floor (neither clearly clears the single-tree-destination exception), written up as data/leads/munzenberg.json (Eiche an der Kirche, WEAK) and data/leads/passau.json (Friedenslinde, UNCLEAR, recommended as a future Passau city seed instead). Both removed from this leads list. 2026-09-03 third follow-up verify pass (cluster check): geographic analysis flagged three 'geleitete Linden' (guided/trained lime tree, a recognised regional folk-tree type) as a possible tight cluster in the Malsfeld/Felsberg/Knüllwald corner of Schwalm-Eder-Kreis, Hessen: Geleitete Linden Berndshausen, Geleitete Linden Dagobertshausen and Tanzlinde (Hilgershausen). All three verified alive and confirmed via baumkunde.de plus a second source each (LAGIS Hessen's historic-sites register for Berndshausen; the Wikimedia Commons gallery page 'Geleitete Linden im Schwalm-Eder-Kreis' for the other two), and genuinely close together (Berndshausen-Dagobertshausen 4.6km, Dagobertshausen-Hilgershausen 3.5km, Berndshausen-Hilgershausen 6.6km). That Commons gallery page turned out to be a real, named regional grouping (12 surviving 'geleitete Linden' across the district) rather than an invented theme, and it named a fourth specimen, the Tanzlinde of Ostheim (Malsfeld), which sits 2.0-4.0km from the other three and was independently verified the same way; it was not previously in this leads file. All four cleared the 4-tree floor as a genuine walkable-by-car cluster and were delivered to data/research/schwalm-eder-linden-verified.json (sel_001 to sel_004). The three that had lead entries here (Berndshausen, Dagobertshausen, Hilgershausen) are removed from this leads list accordingly. Other district members of the same named grouping (Dorflinde Lischeid, Dorflinde Sebbeterode, Kandelaberlinde Dorla, Tanzlinde Niedenstein) were checked for distance and are 18 to 35km from this cluster, too far to join it; they remain as separate leads. Two other Hessian lime candidates in this file, Dorflinde in Aua (Neuenstein) and Gerichtslinde Erdmannrode, were checked and are 15.5km and 33.5km from the cluster respectively, also too far to join it; left as leads. Tanzlinde (Himmelsberg), also in this file, is a different tree from Tanzlinde (Hilgershausen) despite the similar name, and sits about 45km away; left as a lead, flagged in sel_003's verify_notes to avoid future confusion between the two. 2026-09-04 verify pass (famous-germany batch G1, 1 candidate): Riesenbuche bei Altmugl is a duplicate, already known via the Bavarian Naturdenkmale register as reg_bayern-naturdenkmale_1613 (Naturdenkmal Nr.24 Alte Buche bei Altmugl, Mkt. Neualbenreuth, same coordinates). Not a new find; removed from this leads list, no write-up needed. 2026-09-04 verify pass (famous-germany batch H1, 8 candidates): Hranicni buk (Cinovec) is in the Czech Republic, not Germany (Dubi, Ustecky kraj), and its original tree died in the 1970s (lightning) with only a young 2007 replacement sapling alive today; blocked on both grounds, removed from leads. Hutbuche bei Frauenroth confirmed dead, collapsed in Storm Egon Jan 2017; blocked, removed from leads. Urbuche (Mitgenfeld) confirmed dead, broke apart May 2013; blocked, removed from leads. Baerenwaldeiche bei Niederholzklau confirmed dead, fell in storm April 2024; blocked, removed from leads. Dr. August Köster-Eiche (Wuppertal) is a young 2000s memorial oak honouring a local civic-association chairman, no independent fame or age found; blocked as not remarkable enough, removed from leads. 2026-09-05 verify pass (famous-germany batch 2026-09-05-c, 6 candidates): Gerichtslinde Goettingen and Gerichtslinde Scheessel both verified and CLEAR the single-tree-destination bar (real, dated, individually-documented judicial history plus recent alive-now evidence); delivered to data/research/famousgermany-2026-09-05-c-verified.json as deu_famous_001 and deu_famous_002. Removed from this leads list accordingly. Everseiche verified (two sources agree on ~400-450y, 7.2-7.6m girth, Naturdenkmal since 1958) but held: no fame beyond ordinary farm-oak history, and its health is actively declining (baumkunde.de: crown 'appears dead from a distance' by Sept 2024; a directly-fetched July 2025 Commons photo caption confirms it is 'partially dead'). Lieveneiche verified as existing (named after Wilhelm Ferdinand Lieven, Hilden benefactor) but too thin and too unremarkable to clear the bar: no age, no girth, no ND register entry found, held as a lead. Gerichtslinde in Alfeld (Leine) verified but held: the OFFICIAL register lists it as '2 Dinglinden' (ND-HI 135), not one tree, with real but loosely-dated 18th-century judicial history and no age/girth found; corrected in this file's entry and kept as a lead. Heinrichslinde BLOCKED: the current physical tree is a sapling planted January 2022, the second of two prior Heinrichslinden having collapsed (1894) and been felled (2021) respectively; no genuinely old tree stands at the site today, moved to the blocked list. 2026-09-05 follow-up: deu_famous_001 (Gerichtslinde of Goettingen) turned out to be a DUPLICATE of the already-published gtn_001 (Gerichtslinde Gottingen, same coordinates, same girth 714cm, same two sources), caught by passcheck.py --pending before any write pass touched it. Removed from famousgermany-2026-09-05-c-verified.json; no lead entry needed since it is already a published tree under a different id. 2026-09-05 verify pass (famous-germany priority batch, by-demand order): Kaiserlinde (Elversberg) BLOCKED, the historic tree blew over in a March 2015 storm and the current tree at the site is a young sapling planted January 2021 (not the famous old linden); moved to blocked list. Hindenburglinde (Ramsau) verified and shipped as its own single-tree place, a Nationalerbe-Baum (National Heritage Tree Nr. 18) beside the B305 near Ramsau bei Berchtesgaden, girth 10.85m (measured June 2025), age disputed 400-1000y across sources; delivered to data/research/ramsau-verified.json (rsb_001). Removed from this leads list accordingly. 2026-09-07 verify pass (famous-germany batch, 4 candidates): Eichenniederwald Darlingerode BLOCKED, it is a whole protected coppice woodland (Flaechennaturdenkmal since 1973) on the Kapitelsberg near Darlingerode, not a single tree; moved to blocked list. Erinnerungseiche an die Völkerschlacht bei Leipzig (Berga/Elster) verified: a genuine, separately-documented 1863 memorial oak (Naturdenkmal, own information board), distinct from Berga's older Stadteiche/Wappeneiche a few hundred metres away; delivered to data/research/famousgermany-verified.json as dgy_001 (flagged: no girth found, most recent tree photo is 2019, location approximate from a Komoot community coordinate). Removed from this leads list. Jahrhunderteiche (Barmer Wald, Wuppertal) verified: an individually named, individually documented 1908 memorial oak with its own Wikipedia article, physical plaque, precise landmark coordinates and an active custodian association (Barmer Verschoenerungsverein) still running guided walks to it as of Dec 2025; delivered to data/research/famousgermany-verified.json as dgy_002 (flagged: no current girth, only a historical 1908 figure which was deliberately not carried into girth_cm; no photo newer than 2008 checked). Removed from this leads list. Schlosseiche bei Eisolzried (Bergkirchen, Landkreis Dachau, Bavaria) verified: a nationally documented monumental oak, one of the ten thickest single-stem oaks in Germany per the Deutsches Baumarchiv, official Naturdenkmal since 1997, field-remeasured alive and in good condition by monumentale-eichen.de in 2017 (girth grown from 8.00m in 1900/1990 to 9.60m in 2017); delivered to data/research/famousgermany-verified.json as dgy_003 (flagged: age disagreement 350-700y across sources, recorded as a range rather than picked; a 2009 root-damage/endangerment claim from a nearby building not independently re-checked this pass). Removed from this leads list.

leads.name: Königslinde (Invalidenfriedhof Berlin)
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.reason: 2026-09-06 verify pass: DEAD/REMOVED, not a candidate. The original Königslinde on the Invalidenfriedhof (associated with Frederick the Great visiting the Invalidenhaus) was felled when the Berlin Wall's border installations (death strip, control strip, dog run) were built through the cemetery grounds during the GDR period. A NEW tree was planted at the site after reunification once the walled-up section reopened. The current tree is a young replacement, not the historic specimen; the 1897 photograph on Commons shows the original, already gone. Sources: dieterwunderlich.de and gedenktafeln-in-berlin.de both describe the felling and replanting. Never ship as an ancient/veteran tree; could appear as historical context inside another Berlin tree's story per the dead-tree-as-context rule, never as its own entry.

Planted around 1990, so roughly 35 years old today: young trees, not ancient or individually distinguished, exactly analogous to this same file's already-blocked 'Symbolic oaks in Germany' category entry. leads.name: Freiheitslinde Lindaufeld
leads.reason: Real and documented: planted 1898 for the 50th anniversary of the Schleswig-Holstein Uprising (1848-1851), part of a regional series of similar 50th-anniversary freedom memorials (usually paired oaks with a memorial stone) put up across Schleswig-Holstein that year, per Wikimedia Commons categorisation (Gedenksteine zur Schleswig-Holsteinischen Erhebung). Not documented on the town of Boren's own German Wikipedia page at all. This is one of many broadly similar commemorative trees from the same 1898 wave rather than an individually famous specimen: modest age (~128 years), no distinctive girth or form, no dedicated article. Held: a real memorial, not a single-tree destination.

Two independent sources (en.wikipedia, baumkunde.de) agree on species, age and size; publicly accessible.

leads.name: Langenstadt Tanzlinde
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.reason: Real and actively used: the original large Tanzlinde was destroyed in a storm and replaced; the current young linden (girth only 0.87m) has had its branches trained sideways onto the historic rondell of 8 sandstone columns since 2010, when the annual Kirchweih dance tradition (last weekend of August) resumed. The real attraction here is the surviving 18th-century stone dance-floor structure and the revived custom, not the tree itself, which is still young and unremarkable on its own terms; no dedicated Wikipedia article or national designation found (unlike Peesten and Limmersdorf, which shipped this pass). Held: worth revisiting once the replacement tree has grown into the frame, or if the custom itself earns wider recognition.

leads.name: Winterlinde am Friedhof
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.reason: 2026-09-07 verify pass: CONFIRMED DEAD. German Wikipedia's own article (Winterlinde am Friedhof, Eschelbronn) states the tree was felled in October 2019 after a Brandkrustenpilz (Kretzschmaria deusta) fungal infection caused rot at the base and roots; a certified tree inspector assessed it as a public-safety risk ahead of the autumn/winter storm season and it was sawn down piece by piece. Two pieces of a fork went to a local woodturner for display in the village's Schreinermuseum. A sister Naturdenkmal lime at Bettweg (Alte Linde) also came down, in April 2025. Blocked per the never-publish-a-dead-tree rule; moved to blocked list.

leads.name: Everseiche
leads.note: VERIFIED (existence, species, age, coordinates via two independent sources: monumentale-eichen.de and baumkunde.de, both giving matching girth ~7.2-7.6m and 400-450y age; also a Naturdenkmal since 1958 per monumentale-eichen.de) but does NOT clear the single-tree-destination bar. It is a fine large old oak on a green space by the Hase river at the former Everskotten/Gut Eversburg (farm-oak history, nothing more dramatic), with no record-holding claim or documented dramatic history beyond ordinary farm-oak status. WORSE, its health is actively declining and worth flagging hard for whoever revisits: baumkunde.de logs 'numerous dead branches' by Feb 2021 and by its last visit (21 Sep 2024) says only a little green remains and 'the crown appears dead from a distance'. A directly-fetched Commons photo caption dated 9 July 2025 confirms this in the tree's own words: 'Der Baum ist zum Teil schon abgestorben, nur an einigen unteren Zweigen ist noch Laubbesatz' (the tree is partially dead, with foliage only on some lower branches). NOT known dead (some foliage remains as of July 2025), so not blocked outright, but this is a poor 'go see this' pitch right now and a bad candidate for a page promising an epic, thriving tree. A caution on an earlier WebSearch AI-summary claim of '800-1000 years old': that figure appears nowhere on either directly-fetched source page and is discarded per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule; both real sources agree on 400-450 years.

leads.name: Lieveneiche
leads.note: Existence and general identity (an old oak in the Hildener Stadtwald/Hildener Heide area, named after 19th-century Hilden benefactor Wilhelm Ferdinand Lieven, who bequeathed the city its forest on his 1902 death) confirmed across multiple independent sources (de.wikipedia's Wilhelm Ferdinand Lieven article, a hiking-route blog post naming it as a waypoint, komoot listings), but there is no age, no girth, no official Naturdenkmal register listing found for it specifically (checked Wikipedia's Kreis Mettmann Naturdenkmal category, which lists only Stinkesberg and Tillmannsdorfer Sattel, not this tree), and no alive-now evidence more recent than 2016-dated Commons photographs. Missing age is fine per the rules, but there is no fame beyond a local honorific naming, so it fails the single-tree-destination test outright: nobody travels to Hilden for this tree, it is a minor waypoint on a local hiking route. Held as a lead rather than blocked, since nothing here suggests it is dead or inaccessible, just under-documented and unremarkable relative to the bar.

leads.name: Gerichtslinde in Alfeld (Leine)
leads.species: Lime (Tilia sp., unspecified in the register)
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
leads.note:
IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief: this is officially TWO trees, not one. The Naturdenkmal register (de.wikipedia's Liste der Naturdenkmale in Alfeld (Leine)) lists this site as '2 Dinglinden' (a pair of assembly/thing-lindens), ND-HI 135, at 'Alfeld-Nord / Auf dem alten Friedhof an der Hildesheimer Strasse', coordinates 51.98961, 9.82419 (register) vs 51.99065, 9.82543 (a directly-fetched, dated 21 Sept 2025 Commons photo caption placing it on the old cemetery in Alfeld an der Leine) vs 51.9907615, 9.8253568 (the brief's own coordinate); all within about 150m of each other, consistent with one site. A second independent source (alt-alfeld.de, a local-history site) corroborates: the plaza served as a Landgericht site 'noch im 18. Jahrhundert' (still in the 18th century) under 'maechtigen Linden' (mighty lindens, plural, matching the register's two lindens), before part of the plaza became a cemetery in 1609 and continued burials until 1917. Photographs of 'the old court linden' from 1912, 1958 and 1985 are referenced on alt-alfeld.de, and the 21-Sept-2025 Commons photo is recent alive-now evidence.

Does NOT clearly clear the single-tree-destination bar: no age, no girth found anywhere for this specific pair (register gives none), and the judicial-history claim is looser than Goettingen's or Scheesel's (a general 18th-century court under mighty lindens rather than a documented individual-tree role with a specific dated event like an execution). It also being two trees rather than one, per the register-twins rule, would need to ship as a single folded entry rather than one point if it ever ships. Held as a lead for whichever pass looks at Alfeld, or as extra depth if a nearby city is ever opened; do not treat the 18th-century date as this individual tree's age without a source that says so explicitly (bridge-claim risk noted and avoided).

blocked.name: Pücklersche Blutbuche (Muskau Park)
blocked.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species
blocked.reason: DEAD. The original copper beech, transplanted to Bad Muskau by Fuerst Pueckler in 1826 (already 40 years old then, so roughly 250 years old total), died of fungal disease; baumkunde.de records it under the heading † Fuerst-Pueckler-Blutbuche am Schloss Muskau (the dagger denotes deceased in German tree registers). A cutting was planted into the dead trunk/torso and is reportedly growing (baumkunde.de also separately lists a "tote Buche, die noch lebt" entry for the same spot), but that successor is a young, unmeasured sapling with no independent verification of size or age, so it does not itself meet this project's bar yet. No other individually named, verifiable remarkable tree was found in Fuerst-Pueckler-Park Bad Muskau on this pass beyond a row of three unnamed Canadian poplars (planted 1830, not a single collectible point); a Bad Muskau cluster was NOT assembled. A future pass could revisit the successor beech once it has some age/size to verify, or search harder for other named Muskau Park specimens.

One caveat for whoever places this on a city page: it is ~16km from Bamberg centre in a rural part of the Fraenkische Schweiz with NO passenger rail (the branch line to Heiligenstadt closed in 1968); it is reachable by car in roughly 25 minutes but not confirmed within CLAUDE.md's ~30-minute public-transport day-trip boundary, so label the travel time honestly rather than presenting it as an easy add-on to the Wildensorg walk.

blocked.name: Hraniční buk (Cínovec)
blocked.reason: WRONG COUNTRY plus DEAD. Cinovec/Zinnwald-Georgenfeld is a Czech-German border crossing but the tree itself, per cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hranicni_buk_(Cinovec), stands at 50.7330N 13.7686E in Dubi, Teplice district, Ustecky kraj, CZECH REPUBLIC (not Germany); it should not be researched or delivered as a German lead at all, and belongs (if anywhere) in a Czech leads file. Separately and independently disqualifying: the original beech (traditionally dated to a 1537 planting, allegedly rested under by Napoleon) died after 1945, was down to its last living branch by the 1960s, and was finished off by a lightning strike in the 1970s. A replacement beech was planted at the site 2007-08-18 with an information plaque, but it is a young sapling (order of 15-20 years old) with no independent remarkability of its own, comparable to the rejected Kanzelbuche and Puecklersche Blutbuche entries already blocked in this file. Never ship the original; the replacement could be reconsidered decades from now once it has real size, and only as a Czech, not German, candidate.

blocked.name: Hutbuche bei Frauenroth
blocked.reason: DEAD. Per de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hutbuche_bei_Frauenroth and baumkunde.de (which titles its own entry with a dagger, "† Hutebuche in Frauenroth", the German tree-register convention for deceased), this triple-trunked beech stood at the forest edge near the cemetery of Frauenroth (Burkardroth, Bad Kissingen district, Bavaria), designated Naturdenkmal 672-N/030 since 1971, roughly 250-350 years old, and host to an annual Hutbuchenfest. A branch failure in 2009 revealed fungal decay (oyster, honey and fire fungus), and the tree collapsed outright during Storm Egon on the night of 2017-01-12/13. No living successor was found in this search. Never ship.

blocked.name: Urbuche
blocked.reason: DEAD. This European beech stood above Mitgenfeld (part of Oberleichtersbach, Bad Kissingen district, Bavarian Rhoen), on the south slope of the Pilsterberg at roughly 530m elevation, reputed over 600 years old and one of the oldest beeches in Germany, listed as a Naturdenkmal. Per de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbuche, baumkunde.de (again titled with the dagger, deceased marker: "† Urbuche bei Mitgenfeld") and infranken.de news coverage, it broke apart on the night of 2013-05-13/14, shortly after inspectors had found a crack and were planning to brace the crown. Photos on Commons (2020) likely show the site or remnants rather than a living tree; treat any post-2013 photo with suspicion if this is ever reconsidered. Never ship.

blocked.name: Bärenwaldeiche bei Niederholzklau
blocked.reason: DEAD. This pedunculate oak (Quercus robur) stood in forest near Niederholzklau (part of Freudenberg, Siegen-Wittgenstein, North Rhine-Westphalia), first documented 1453, reputed roughly 700 years old, about 5m girth and 30m tall, Naturdenkmal since 1988, damaged by a lightning strike in 1990 (bark stripped along 20m) and treated with mycorrhizal soil inoculation from 1993. Per de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baerenwaldeiche, baumkunde.de (dagger-marked deceased) and siegener-zeitung.de/freudenberg-online.com news coverage, it fell in a storm on the night of 2024-04-15 and is confirmed dead. Never ship.

blocked.name: Dr. August Köster-Eiche
blocked.reason: NOT REMARKABLE. This is a young memorial oak in the Ronsdorfer Anlagen park, Wuppertal (roughly 51.234N 7.207E), honouring Dr. August Köster, who chaired the Ronsdorfer Heimat- und Buergerverein (local heritage/civic association) 1935-1966. Wikimedia Commons categorises the tree under "planted in the 2000s" (its own subcategory carries no Wikidata item and no age/girth data), it does not appear in de.wikipedia's own "Liste der Gedenkbaeume in Wuppertal", and no source found gives it any age, size or independent fame beyond the memorial sign. A tree honouring a local association chairman, itself only about two decades old, does not clear the genuinely-old / visually-spectacular / historically-significant bar and clearly fails the single-tree-destination test (nobody would travel specifically for this tree). Wuppertal is not yet a published city; this candidate is not strong enough to seed one and would not survive as a lead worth carrying forward either. Photographs (Commons, 2015) not inspected further since the tree fails on remarkability before location or photo quality become relevant.

blocked.name: Heinrichslinde
blocked.reason: No genuinely old tree exists at this site today. Confirmed dead/removed twice over: the original Heinrichslinde (Tilia platyphyllos, legendarily linked to Heinrich der Loewe c.1173, first documented 1492, reached 6.30m girth) collapsed 19 September 1894. Its successor (a winter linden planted after failed 1861/1862 attempts) stood until it was FELLED on 18 November 2021 due to rot and fungal damage. A third tree was planted in its place in January 2022, meaning the CURRENT physical specimen on the Domplatz is only about 4 years old as of 2026: a sapling, not a collectible ancient/veteran tree. Two independent sources confirm this timeline (de.wikipedia's Heinrichslinde article, directly fetched, and der-loewe.info's own 'die neue Heinrichslinde steht' and 'fake news' articles, also directly fetched). The brief's suspicion about the 1885 Gartenlaube engravings was correct: those are illustrations, not photographs, and irrelevant to the current tree's condition regardless. Also worth flagging for any future writer: der-loewe.info's fake-news piece argues the entire 1173-planting-by-Heinrich-der-Loewe legend is itself unsupported (the Domplatz was a construction site in 1173 with no room for a tree), so even the site's founding legend is disputed, on top of the current tree being a 2022 sapling. Blocked as a collectible entry; the site's continuity story could still be mentioned as context inside some other Braunschweig tree's page, never as its own entry, per the dead-tree-as-context rule.

blocked.name: Kaiserlinde (Elversberg)
blocked.reason: Dead. The historic Kaiserlinde (planted 1871 or 1913) blew over in a storm in March 2015 and was never restorable. A new linden, already ~20 years old at time of planting, was donated and planted at the same spot in January 2021 (Lindenstrasse/Waldstrasse corner, Spiesen-Elversberg). The current physical tree is a young replacement (roughly 5 years in the ground as of 2026), not the famous old tree; no honest ancient-tree entry can be made for it today. Sources: de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaiserlinde_(Elversberg), blaulichtreport-saarland.de 2015 storm-loss report.

blocked.name: Eichenniederwald Darlingerode (NDM)
blocked.reason: BLOCKED: not a collectible tree. The Naturdenkmal 'Eichen Niederwald' (designated 1973) protects a whole oak coppice woodland (Eichenschaelwald) on the Kapitelsberg hill near Darlingerode, Harz, Sachsen-Anhalt, a Flaechennaturdenkmal (area monument) covering remnants of historic coppice forestry (crooked, multi-stemmed oaks throughout the stand), not one identifiable specimen. Confirmed via de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapitelsberg_(Darlingerode) ("Er gehoert zum seit 1973 bestehenden Flaechennaturdenkmal Eichen Niederwald") and the Wikimedia Commons category description. Fails the one-collectible-point rule (BRIEF_RESEARCH.md hard limits): an avenue or a whole wood is blocked.
